svg.title: P013 · States with at least five customers
svg.desc: One row per state group with at least five customers. IDs 1–5 form Karnataka, ID 6 forms Maharashtra, IDs 7–11 form NULL and IDs 12–17 form Delhi. Four groups become three. Maharashtra has one customer. Karnataka and NULL qualify with exactly five, and NULL displays as Unknown. Delhi's six come first. The two groups of five sort by the displayed labels Karnataka and Unknown.
svg.text: States with at least five customers
One row per state group with at least five customers.
Five customers have no recorded state. Will their group meet the threshold?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
How many customers belong to each state?
IDs 1–5 form Karnataka, ID 6 forms Maharashtra, IDs 7–11 form NULL and IDs 12–17 form Delhi.
Which state groups meet the threshold?
Four groups become three. Maharashtra has one customer. Karnataka and NULL qualify with exactly five, and NULL
Which state wins a tie on customer count?
Delhi's six come first. The two groups of five sort by the displayed labels Karnataka and Unknown.
ORDER BY COUNT(CustomerID) DESC, State ASC
